# MeshWeave

> AI Agent Visibility Audit — see how AI reads your website, and fix what matters first.

MeshWeave helps teams understand what AI agents can make of their website. It crawls a
site as a machine reader would, checks the signals available to an agent, and turns the
findings into a prioritized list of improvements.

Free web app: https://meshweaveai.com/ · Free JSON API (see below) · Open source:
https://github.com/malvavisc0/meshweave

## What problem it solves

Search is no longer limited to a list of links. Buyers increasingly ask AI agents to
explain a category, compare vendors, or suggest what to do next. A site can have good
search fundamentals and still be difficult for an agent to use: a long marketing paragraph
may hide the answer, a missing `Organization` schema may leave the business identity
ambiguous, an email buried on a legal page may not look like a useful next step.

MeshWeave looks at the layer after discovery: whether an AI agent can accurately
understand, extract, trust, cite, and use what the site says.

## The three lenses

Each audit answers three questions, scored separately so the fix for one failure mode is
never confused with another:

- **AEO — Answer Engine Optimization** (`Poor` → `Excellent`): Can an agent find and
  extract the answer a buyer needs? Looks at schema coverage, heading hierarchy, content
  structure, dates, and image alt text.
- **GEO — Generative Engine Optimization** (`Invisible` → `Dominant`): Does the site
  give an agent enough consistent, credible evidence to trust and recommend the
  business? Looks at Organization schema, entity consistency, E-E-A-T signals, AI
  crawler access (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot), `robots.txt`, sitemaps, and
  `llms.txt`.
- **AAX — AI Agent Experience** (`Opaque` → `Fluent`): Can an agent understand the offer
  and find a credible next step? Homepage comprehension, meta optimization, cross-page
  content consistency, email contacts, and contact paths.

## API integration (free)

The public JSON API returns the same analysis shown on the site. No key required
today; an API key plan (free tier + paid tiers) is planned. Responses are JSON except
`POST /submit`, which answers with a 303 redirect. No authentication is required for
public analyses.

### Analyze a site (anonymous submission)

```
POST {base}/submit
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

mode=site&domain=example.com
```

Anonymous submissions are public; max 10 pages, depth 1. Authenticated submissions
(via browser session) can be private, up to 25 pages by default (250 cap, depth 3).

The response is a redirect to the analysis page — for API use, follow the redirect and
extract the crawl id or short key, then poll:

### Check analysis status

```
GET {base}/api/status/{crawl_id}
```

Returns `{status: "pending"|"running"|"succeeded"|"failed", error, report_url}`. Public
analyses also include a short `key`. Poll until `succeeded`, then use the key below.

### Get the analysis (public)

```
GET {base}/api/analysis/public/{key}
GET {base}/api/analysis/public/{key}/summary
```

Returns headline scores (AEO, GEO, AAX composites + ratings), a risk summary
(profile, headline, diagnosis), finding count, and counts (pages, emails, links). The
public payload is intentionally curated: raw emails, full page bodies, recommendation
guidance, and the full score snapshot are owner-only.

### List analyses for a domain

```
GET {base}/api/domain/{domain}
```

Returns up to 100 public entries with keys and status.

### Health

```
GET {base}/healthz    → {"status": "ok"}
GET {base}/readyz     → checks DB + OAuth readiness
```

## Notes for agents and integrators

- Full private payloads (complete factors, recommendations, score snapshots) require a
  browser-authenticated owner session; an API-key regime is planned. For programmatic
  access today, use public analyses or contact us.
- `robots.txt` at {base} declares AI crawlers welcome; the site serves this
  `llms.txt` and a fuller `llms-full.txt` at {base}/.well-known/llms-full.txt.
- Rate limits: anonymous crawls are capped server-side (10 pages default); signed-in
  users get higher quotas. If you need bulk or commercial usage, email us first.
